title: Week 5
priceNote: Prices are estimates of regular Publix shelf prices at Lakeside Commons in Milledgeville (store 2003) and do not include tax. BOGO and sale prices are checked on publix.com when a week is written. Sunday's turkey meatballs go Italian, teriyaki and Moroccan across ten portions, and one pot of marinara carries four meals.
allergyNote: Nothing on this plan contains tree nuts or fish. Moroccan tagines are often topped with toasted nuts; this one uses golden raisins and cilantro instead. Peanut butter is often made in plants that also handle tree nuts. If your allergy is strict, check the label for a 'may contain tree nuts' line.
weekendNote: Festival days. Leftovers waiting for you: a bowl of meatball tagine with couscous.
snacks: Cottage cheese with a drizzle of honey

have.name: Peanut butter
have.note: about a quarter of the jar

mon.heads: Everything today comes from Sunday's prep. Dinner makes Wednesday's lunch.

tue.heads: Dinner is 10 minutes in the air fryer after pickleball.

wed.heads: Tonight, move the 5 frozen meatball portions to the fridge and cook 1 cup of rice for tomorrow. Dinner makes Thursday's lunch.

thu.heads: Fried rice wants yesterday's rice. It makes Friday's lunch.

prep.title: Sunday batch prep
prep.makes: About 60 turkey meatballs (10 portions), 7 cups of marinara, teriyaki sauce, 2 trays of roasted vegetables, rice, 3 jars of oats, 6 eggs
steps: Start the marinara first. It simmers for 20 minutes while you do everything else.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Chop the broccoli, zucchini, peppers, red onion and 1 sweet potato and toss them for the roasting trays.
Mix the meatballs and roll about 60 of them onto 2 sprayed sheet pans. Bake 16 to 18 minutes.
Turn the oven up to 425°F and roast the vegetables on the same 2 pans for 25 minutes, swapping them halfway.
Cook 1½ cups of rice and simmer the teriyaki sauce for 3 minutes.
Mix 3 jars of apple cinnamon oats. Air-fry 6 eggs at 270°F for 15 minutes.
Portion the meatballs 6 to a container. Fridge 5 (2 teriyaki bowls, 2 for the ziti, 1 for subs).
Freeze the other 5 (2 for fried rice, 3 for the tagine). Cooked meatballs keep 3 to 4 days, so the end of the week waits in the freezer.
Pack 2 teriyaki bowls. Keep the sauces in jars.

prep.title: Wednesday night
prep.makes: Chicken parm for two, Thursday's lunch and rice for fried rice
steps: Move the 5 frozen meatball portions to the fridge.
Cook 1 cup of rice, spread it on a plate to cool and refrigerate it uncovered. Cold, dry rice fries best.
Make the chicken parm and keep the third cutlet for Thursday's sub.

turkey-meatballs.name: Sheet-pan turkey meatballs
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and spray 2 sheet pans with cooking spray.
In a big bowl, mix the 2 eggs, 1 cup oats, ½ cup parmesan, grated onion, grated garlic, 1 tsp garlic powder, 2½ tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper. Let it sit 5 minutes so the oats soften.
Add the ground turkey and mix with your hands until just combined. Overmixing makes them tough.
Roll into about 60 balls the size of a golf ball, 30 to a pan.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until they reach 165°F inside.
Cool, then pack 6 to a container. Fridge 5, freeze 5.
turkey-meatballs.tip: Seasoned plainly on purpose, so they can go marinara, teriyaki or Moroccan later in the week. The oats replace breadcrumbs and keep them juicy.

marinara.name: Big-pot marinara
steps: Soften the diced onion in 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat for 6 minutes.
Add the sliced garlic, 1 tbsp Italian seasoning and a pinch of red pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Pour in both cans of crushed tomatoes with 1 tsp honey and 1½ tsp salt.
Simmer 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens a little.
Cool and keep in jars. It keeps a week in the fridge.
marinara.tip: The honey takes the tinny edge off canned tomatoes.

teriyaki.name: Honey garlic teriyaki sauce
steps: Whisk 1 tbsp cornstarch into ¼ cup cold water.

In a small pot, combine ½ cup soy sauce, ⅓ cup honey, 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 3 grated garlic cloves, 1 tsp ground ginger, 1 tsp toasted sesame oil and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Bring it to a simmer.
Whisk in the cornstarch water and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until glossy and thick.
Cool and keep in a jar.

roast-veg.name: Two-tray roasted vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.

Toss the broccoli crowns, zucchini, bell peppers, red onion and sweet potato with 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1½ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper. Spread it over 2 sheet pans so nothing is crowded.
Roast 25 minutes, swapping the pans and stirring halfway, until browned at the edges.
Cool, then store in one big container.
roast-veg.tip: Seasoned without herbs this week so it works with marinara and teriyaki alike.

apple-oats.name: Apple pie overnight oats
steps: Stir 1½ cups milk, 1½ cups yogurt, 3 tbsp peanut butter, 1 tbsp honey, 1½ tsp ground cinnamon and a pinch of salt together.
Stir in 1½ cups oats and 3 tbsp raisins and split across 3 jars.
Top each with diced apple.
Keeps 4 days. Eat cold, or warm it 90 seconds for a December morning.

marinara-eggs.name: Eggs in marinara with a crusty roll
steps: Warm the marinara in a small skillet and stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Make 3 wells and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook on medium-low for 5 to 6 minutes, until the whites set and the yolks stay soft.
Finish with 1 tbsp parmesan, a pinch of red pepper flakes and black pepper to taste, and scoop it up with the toasted roll.
marinara-eggs.tip: Sunday's marinara turns into a 10-minute breakfast.

hb-eggs.name: Air-fryer hard-boiled eggs
steps: Put the eggs straight into the air fryer basket.
Cook at 270°F for 15 minutes.
Move them to a bowl of ice water for 5 minutes, then refrigerate.
Peel and sprinkle with salt to eat.

teriyaki-bowl.name: Teriyaki meatball rice bowl
steps: Toss each portion of meatballs in 3 tbsp teriyaki sauce.
Pack ¾ cup rice, 1 cup roasted vegetables and the meatballs in each container.
Reheat 2 minutes, then top with green onion and a few drops of sesame oil.
teriyaki-bowl.tip: Built from Sunday's meatballs, vegetables and teriyaki.

baked-ziti.name: Meatball baked ziti
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Boil the penne in salted water 2 minutes short of the box time and drain.
Stir the pasta with the marinara, meatballs, roasted vegetables, spinach and cottage cheese right in the cast iron.
Top with mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake 15 minutes, then broil 2 minutes until the cheese browns.
Pack half for Wednesday's lunch.
baked-ziti.tip: Cottage cheese melts into the sauce like ricotta and adds about 14g of protein a serving.

meatball-subs.name: Air-fryer meatball subs
steps: Warm the meatballs in the marinara for 2 minutes in the microwave.
Split the rolls and fill each with 3 meatballs and sauce.
Top with mozzarella, parmesan and Italian seasoning.
Air-fry at 380°F for 4 minutes until the cheese bubbles and the rolls crisp.
meatball-subs.tip: The fastest dinner of the week, for after Tuesday pickleball.

chicken-parm.name: Air-fryer chicken parmesan
steps: Pound the chicken cutlets to an even ½ inch and season with ½ tsp salt.
Beat the egg in a shallow bowl. In another, mix 1 cup panko breadcrumbs, half the parmesan (about 3 tbsp), 1 tsp Italian seasoning and ½ tsp garlic powder.
Dip each cutlet in the egg, then press it into the panko mix.
Spray the basket and the cutlets with cooking spray and air-fry at 400°F for 10 minutes, flipping halfway.
Spoon about ½ cup marinara over the cutlets, top with ¾ cup mozzarella and the rest of the parmesan, and air-fry 2 minutes more.
Meanwhile, boil 6 oz penne, toss it with ¾ cup warm marinara and reheat 2 cups roasted vegetables.
Wrap the third cutlet for Thursday with the last ¼ cup marinara. Tuck it into the toasted roll for a chicken parm sub.
chicken-parm.tip: Date-night comfort food for two, and it makes Thursday's lunch.

teriyaki-fried-rice.name: Teriyaki meatball fried rice
steps: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in the cast iron until shimmering. Sear the quartered turkey meatballs 2 minutes and push them aside.
Scramble the 3 eggs in the empty space, then add the garlic, 1 cup frozen peas and carrots and the chopped roasted vegetables for 1 minute.
Add the cold rice, press it flat and leave it 2 minutes to crisp.
Toss with ¼ cup teriyaki sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp sesame oil.
Finish with green onion. Pack half for Friday's lunch.
teriyaki-fried-rice.tip: Dinner after Thursday pickleball. Wednesday's rice makes it crisp, not mushy.

meatball-tagine.name: Moroccan meatball tagine with couscous
meatball-tagine.equip: cast iron with a lid, pot

ingredients.qty: 1½ cups plus 1¼ cups for the couscous

steps: Soften the sliced onion in 1 tbsp olive oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the 3 cloves garlic, 2 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp ground cinnamon, ½ tsp ground ginger and ½ tsp ground turmeric for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the sweet potatoes, chickpeas, diced tomatoes, ¼ cup raisins and 1½ cups broth. Cover and simmer 12 minutes.
Nestle in the 3 portions of turkey meatballs, cover and simmer 6 minutes more until the sweet potatoes are tender and the meatballs are hot. Taste and season with salt.
Meanwhile, bring 1¼ cups broth to a boil, stir in the couscous with a pinch of salt, cover off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff with the lemon zest.
Finish the tagine with the lemon juice and cilantro, and serve over couscous with a spoon of Greek yogurt.
Pack one bowl for Saturday.
meatball-tagine.tip: This week's new one, and a dinner for two. Warm spices, sweet raisins and lemon make it taste nothing like the rest of the week's meatballs.
